+    def forward(
+        self,
+        input_ids: torch.Tensor,
+        positions: torch.Tensor,
+        intermediate_tensors: IntermediateTensors | None = None,
+        inputs_embeds: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+        lookback_token_ids: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        if self.engram_hash is None:
+            return super().forward(
+                input_ids, positions, intermediate_tensors, inputs_embeds
+            )
+        if input_ids is None:
+            raise ValueError("Flash Engram requires original input token IDs")
+        hidden = (
+            inputs_embeds
+            if inputs_embeds is not None
+            else self.embed_input_ids(input_ids)
+        )
+        hashes = input_ids.new_empty(
+            (
+                len(self.config.engram_layer_ids),
+                input_ids.numel(),
+                self.engram_hash.offsets.shape[1],
+            ),
+            dtype=torch.int32,
+        )
+        self.engram_hash.prepare_hashes_with_output(
+            input_ids,
+            lookback_token_ids,
+            self.layers[0].self_attn.mla_attn.layer_name,
+            hashes,
+        )
+        hash_indices = {
+            layer_id - 1: index
+            for index, layer_id in enumerate(self.config.engram_layer_ids)
+        }
+        for index, layer in enumerate(self.layers):
+            if index in hash_indices:
+                hidden = layer.hc_attn_layer.prepare_input(hidden)
+                hidden = layer.engram_layer(hidden, hashes[hash_indices[index]])

+
+    def _record_part(self, name: str, part: Any) -> None:
+        parts = self.loaded_parts.setdefault(name, set())
+        if part in parts or (None in parts) or (part is None and parts):
+            raise ValueError(f"Duplicate Flash checkpoint weight or shard: {name}")
+        parts.add(part)
+
+    def load_weights(self, weights: Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]) -> set[str]:
+        parameters = dict(self.named_parameters())
+        loaded: set[str] = set()
+        for name, value in weights:
+            engram = re.fullmatch(r"layers\.(\d+)\.engram_layer\.(.+)", name)
+            if engram is not None:
+                assert self.engram_hash is not None
+                layer, leaf = engram.groups()
+                if int(layer) + 1 not in (self.config.engram_layer_ids or ()):
+                    raise ValueError(f"Undeclared Engram checkpoint weight: {name}")
+                if leaf == "lookup_table":
+                    self._record_part(name, None)
+                    self.engram_hash.load_lookup(value)
+                    continue
+                if leaf in (
+                    "multi_head_embedding.embedding.weight",
+                    "multi_head_embedding.embedding.weight_scale_inv",
+                ):
+                    self._record_part(name, None)
+                    embedding = self.layers[
+                        int(layer)
+                    ].engram_layer.multi_head_embedding
+                    embedding.load_weight(leaf.rsplit(".", 1)[1], value)
+                    loaded.add(name)
+                    continue
+            expert = _EXPERT_WEIGHT.fullmatch(name)
+            if expert:
+                prefix, expert_id, projection, suffix = expert.groups()
+                shards = {
+                    "gate_proj": ("w1",),
+                    "up_proj": ("w3",),
+                    "down_proj": ("w2",),
+                    "gate_up_proj": ("w1", "w3"),
+                }[projection]
+                suffix = (suffix or "").removeprefix(".weight")
+                param_name = "w2_weight" if projection == "down_proj" else "w13_weight"
+                target = f"{prefix}.routed_experts.{param_name}{suffix}"
+                if target not in parameters:
+                    raise ValueError(f"Unknown Flash expert weight: {name}")
+                parameter = parameters[target]
+                if expert_id is None:
+                    if value.ndim != 3 or value.shape[0] != self.config.num_experts:
+                        raise ValueError(
+                            f"Invalid packed expert shape for {name}: {value.shape}"
+                        )
+                    expert_ids = list(range(self.config.num_experts))
+                else:
+                    expert_ids = [int(expert_id)]
+                for index in expert_ids:
+                    if not 0 <= index < self.config.num_experts:
+                        raise ValueError(f"Expert index out of range: {name}")
+                    tensor = value[index] if expert_id is None else value
+                    pieces = tensor.chunk(len(shards), dim=-2)
+                    for shard, piece in zip(shards, pieces):
+                        success = parameter.weight_loader(
+                            parameter,
+                            piece,
+                            target,
+                            shard_id=shard,
+                            expert_id=index,
+                            return_success=True,
+                        )
+                        if success:
+                            self._record_part(target, (index, shard))
+                            loaded.add(target)
+                continue
+            if name.endswith((".hc_fn", ".hc_head_fn")):
+                name += ".weight"
+            name = name.replace(".gate.e_score_correction_bias", ".expert_bias")
+            name = name.replace(".router.gate.", ".gate.")
+            if ".engram_layer.lookup_per_head_norms." in name:
+                prefix, suffix = name.split(".lookup_per_head_norms.")
+                head, leaf = suffix.split(".", 1)
+                embedding = self.get_submodule(prefix).multi_head_embedding
+                if not head.isdigit() or not 0 <= int(head) < embedding.n_hash_cols:
+                    raise ValueError(f"Invalid Engram hash head weight: {name}")
+                if not embedding.head_start <= int(head) < embedding.head_end:
+                    continue
+                local_head = int(head) - embedding.head_start
+                name = f"{prefix}.lookup_per_head_norms.{local_head}.{leaf}"
+            if name not in parameters:
+                raise ValueError(f"Unknown Flash checkpoint weight: {name}")
+            parameter = parameters[name]
+            weight_shard = getattr(value, "shard_id", None)
+            self._record_part(name, weight_shard)

+            if weight_shard is None:
+                loader(parameter, value)
+            else:
+                loader(parameter, value, weight_shard)

+
+    def verify_loaded_parts(self) -> None:
+        for layer_id in self.config.engram_layer_ids or ():
+            prefix = f"layers.{layer_id - 1}.engram_layer."
+            required = {
+                prefix + "lookup_table",

+                )

+            if None in parts:
+                continue
+            module_name, _, leaf = name.rpartition(".")
+            module = self.get_submodule(module_name)
+            expected: set[Any]
+            if leaf.startswith(("w13_weight", "w2_weight")):

+                shards = ("w1", "w3") if leaf.startswith("w13_") else ("w2",)
+                expected = {(i, s) for i in local_ids for s in shards}
+            else:
+                expected = set(range(len(module.output_sizes)))

+        outermost = self._weight_loading_depth == 0

+            self.model.loaded_parts.clear()
+            self._seen_weights.clear()

+                required = {

+            self._seen_weights.add(name)

+                name = f"model.layers.{layer_id - 1}.engram_layer.{leaf}"

+                if layer.isdigit() and first <= int(layer) < (

+                                "confidence_head.",
+                            )
+                        )

+                yield name, value
+
+    def load_weights(self, weights: Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]) -> set[str]:

+                self._target_weights(weights), mapper=self.hf_to_vllm_mapper
+            )

+class HYV4FlashMoE(HYV4MoEFused):
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        config: HYV4FlashConfig,
+        quant_config: QuantizationConfig | None,
+        prefix: str,

+        down: nn.Module | None = None
+        up: nn.Module | None = None
+        if latent is not None:

+
+from typing import Any

+import torch

+from vllm.forward_context import get_forward_context
+from vllm.models.hy_v4.nvidia.flashmla_sparse import HYV4FlashMLASparseBackend

+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla.flashmla_sparse import FlashMLASparseMetadataBuilder
+
+
+class FlashSparseMetadataBuilder(FlashMLASparseMetadataBuilder):
+    _cudagraph_support = AttentionCGSupport.UNIFORM_BATCH
+
+    def __init__(self, kv_cache_spec, layer_names, vllm_config, device):
+        super().__init__(kv_cache_spec, layer_names, vllm_config, device)
+        layer = vllm_config.compilation_config.static_forward_context[layer_names[0]]
+        assert layer.topk_buffer_width is not None
+        self.topk_tokens = layer.topk_buffer_width
+        self.topk_tokens_tensor.fill_(self.topk_tokens)
+        # The direct paged kernel never gathers evicted SWA history.
+        self.fp8_use_mixed_batch = True
+
+
+class FlashSparseBackend(HYV4FlashMLASparseBackend):
+    @staticmethod
+    def get_builder_cls():
+        return FlashSparseMetadataBuilder
+
+    @classmethod
+    def supports_pcp(cls):
+        return False
+
+    @classmethod
+    def supports_dcp(cls):
+        return False
+
+
+class FlashSWABackend(FlashSparseBackend):
+    @classmethod
+    def supports_sliding_window(cls):
+        return True
+
+
+def window_indices(positions: torch.Tensor, window: int, width: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    if window < 1 or width < window:
+        raise ValueError("SWA index width must cover its causal window")
+    columns = torch.arange(width, device=positions.device)
+    indices = positions[:, None] - window + 1 + columns
+    live = (positions[:, None] >= 0) & (columns < window) & (indices >= 0)
+    return torch.where(live, indices, -1).int()
+
+
+class FlashWindowIndexer(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, window: int, topk_indices_buffer, attention_prefix: str):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.window = window
+        self.attention_prefix = attention_prefix
+        # Logical-to-physical remapping uses 128-column tiles.
+        width = round_up(window, 128)
+        if window < 1 or topk_indices_buffer.shape[1] < width:
+            raise ValueError("SWA index width must cover its causal window")
+        rows = topk_indices_buffer.shape[0]
+        # Reuse the shared scratch storage with a packed, window-sized stride.
+        self.topk_indices_buffer = topk_indices_buffer.view(-1)[: rows * width].view(
+            rows, width
+        )
+
+    def forward(self, hidden_states, q_c, positions, rope=None):
+        output = self.topk_indices_buffer[: hidden_states.shape[0]]
+        metadata = get_forward_context().attn_metadata
+        if metadata is None:
+            return output.fill_(-1)
+        if not isinstance(metadata, dict):
+            raise TypeError("Flash SWA requires per-layer metadata")
+        meta: Any = metadata[self.attention_prefix]
+        if meta.num_actual_tokens == 0 or meta.seq_lens.numel() == 0:
+            return output.fill_(-1)
+        rows = torch.arange(output.shape[0], device=output.device)
+        starts = meta.query_start_loc
+        requests = torch.searchsorted(starts[1:], rows, right=True)
+        requests = requests.clamp_max(starts.numel() - 2).long()
+        logical = meta.seq_lens[requests] - (starts[requests + 1] - starts[requests])
+        logical = logical + rows - starts[requests]
+        live = (rows < meta.num_actual_tokens) & (rows < starts[-1])
+        output.copy_(
+            window_indices(torch.where(live, logical, -1), self.window, output.shape[1])
+        )
+        return output

+def smart_resize(height, width, factor=32, min_pixels=4096, max_pixels=4194304):
+    if min(height, width, factor, min_pixels) <= 0 or max_pixels < min_pixels:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "Image dimensions and pixel limits must be positive and ordered"
+        )
+    if max(height, width) / min(height, width) > 200:
+        raise ValueError("Image aspect ratio must not exceed 200")
+    h, w = round(height / factor) * factor, round(width / factor) * factor
+    if h * w > max_pixels:
+        scale = math.sqrt(height * width / max_pixels)
+        h = max(factor, math.floor(height / scale / factor) * factor)
+        w = max(factor, math.floor(width / scale / factor) * factor)
+    elif h * w < min_pixels:
+        scale = math.sqrt(min_pixels / (height * width))
+        h = math.ceil(height * scale / factor) * factor
+        w = math.ceil(width * scale / factor) * factor
+    h, w = max(h, factor), max(w, factor)
+    if h * w > max_pixels:
+        raise ValueError("Image aspect ratio and patch rounding exceed max_pixels")
+    return h, w

+    t, channels, height, width = frames.shape
+    if height % patch_size or width % patch_size:
+        raise ValueError("Image dimensions must be divisible by patch_size")
+    return (

+class DFlySpeculatorConfig(DraftModelSpeculatorConfig):
+    """DFly behavior shared by model-specific configuration subclasses."""
+
+    base_method = "dfly"
+    uses_target_hidden_states = True
+    shares_target_positions = False
+    parallel_drafting = True
+
+    @classmethod
+    def default_model(cls, spec: "SpeculativeConfig") -> str:
+        if spec.target_model_config is None:
+            raise ValueError("DFly requires target_model_config")
+        return spec.target_model_config.model
+
+    @classmethod
+    def draft_hf_overrides(
+        cls, spec: "SpeculativeConfig"
+    ) -> Callable[["PreTrainedConfig"], "PreTrainedConfig"]:
+        target = spec.target_model_config
+        if target is None:
+            raise ValueError("DFly requires target_model_config")
+        raise ValueError(
+            "No DFly configuration is registered for target model type "
+            f"{target.hf_text_config.model_type!r}"
+        )
+
+    @classmethod
+    def resolve_num_speculative_tokens(cls, spec: "SpeculativeConfig") -> None:
+        n = spec.num_speculative_tokens
+        if n is None:
+            block_size = getattr(
+                spec.target_model_config.hf_config, "dfly_block_size", None
+            )
+            if type(block_size) is not int or not 2 <= block_size <= 17:
+                raise ValueError("DFly requires dfly_block_size in [2, 17]")
+            # The checkpoint block includes the separate anchor query.
+            n = block_size - 1
+        if type(n) is not int or not 1 <= n <= 16:
+            raise ValueError("DFly requires num_speculative_tokens in [1, 16]")
+        spec.num_speculative_tokens = n
+
+    @classmethod
+    def apply_options(cls, spec: "SpeculativeConfig") -> None:
+        if spec.enable_adaptive_verification:
+            raise ValueError("DFly does not support adaptive verification")
+        if spec.rejection_sample_method != "standard":
+            raise ValueError("DFly requires standard target verification")
+
+    @property
+    def num_lookahead_tokens(self) -> int:
+        return self.num_speculative_tokens + 1
+
+    def max_num_draft_seqs(self, max_num_batched_tokens: int) -> int:
+        return max_num_batched_tokens // self.num_lookahead_tokens

+@pytest.mark.asyncio(loop_scope="module")
+async def test_streaming_input_overflow_chunk_dropped_session_continues(
+    engine: AsyncLLM,
+):
+    """A chunk that would overflow max_model_len gets an empty "length" turn
+    and a later chunk that fits continues the session (#62707)."""
+    request_id = "test_overflow_dropped"
+    sampling_params = get_sampling_params(max_tokens=10)
+
+    # max_model_len is 2048: the second chunk overflows, the third fits.
+    first_chunk = "hello " * 1500
+    overflow_chunk = "world " * 700
+    fitting_chunk = " The end is near and"
+
+    first_turn_done = asyncio.Event()
+    finish_count = 0
+
+    async def input_generator() -> AsyncGenerator[StreamingInput, None]:
+        yield StreamingInput(prompt=first_chunk)
+        yield StreamingInput(prompt=overflow_chunk)
+        await first_turn_done.wait()
+        yield StreamingInput(prompt=fitting_chunk)
+
+    outputs: list[RequestOutput] = []
+    full_text = ""
+
+    async def consume() -> None:
+        nonlocal finish_count, full_text
+        async for output in engine.generate(
+            input_generator(), sampling_params, request_id
+        ):
+            outputs.append(output)
+            if output.outputs and output.outputs[0].text:
+                full_text += output.outputs[0].text
+            if output.outputs and output.outputs[0].finish_reason is not None:
+                finish_count += 1
+                if finish_count == 1:
+                    first_turn_done.set()
+
+    await asyncio.wait_for(consume(), timeout=180)
+
+    assert finish_count == 3
+    assert outputs[-1].finished
+    assert len(full_text) > 0
+    empty_turns = [
+        out
+        for out in outputs
+        if out.outputs
+        and out.outputs[0].finish_reason == "length"
+        and not out.outputs[0].text
+    ]
+    assert len(empty_turns) == 1, "the dropped chunk must end one empty reply"
+    assert not engine.output_processor.has_unfinished_requests()
+

Signed-off-by: cjackal <44624812+cjackal@users.noreply.github.com>

@@ -130,6 +130,21 @@ llm = LLM(
 )
 ```
 
+!!! note
+    If [embedding inputs](../features/multimodal_inputs.md#embedding-inputs) are enabled (`enable_mm_embeds=True`, which EC/KV consumers turn on automatically), a zero limit only disables raw inputs: the modality still accepts pre-computed embeddings and reserves encoder cache space for them.
+    Also set `"allow_embeds": False` to disable it completely:
+
+    ```python
+    from vllm import LLM
+
+    # Accept image embeddings, but neither videos nor video embeddings
+    llm = LLM(
+        model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct",
+        enable_mm_embeds=True,
+        limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 0, "video": {"count": 0, "allow_embeds": False}},
+    )
+    ```
+
 ### Configurable options
 
 `limit_mm_per_prompt` also accepts configurable options per modality. In the configurable form, you still specify `count`, and you may optionally provide size hints that control how vLLM profiles and reserves memory for your multi‑modal inputs. This helps you tune memory for the actual media you expect, instead of the model’s absolute maxima.

+def _exited_cleanly(proc: BaseProcess) -> bool:
+    """Whether `proc` exited with status 0, without reaping it.
+
+    Reading `proc.exitcode` would reap the child, racing `shutdown()`'s join;
+    `WNOWAIT` leaves `shutdown()` as the only reaper. The engine is a direct
+    child under both start methods `get_mp_context()` uses (fork and spawn).
+    """
+    if not hasattr(os, "waitid"):  # macOS before Python 3.13
+        return proc.exitcode == 0
+    try:
+        info = os.waitid(os.P_PID, cast(int, proc.pid), os.WEXITED | os.WNOWAIT)
+    except ChildProcessError:  # already reaped by shutdown()
+        return True
+    return info is not None and info.si_code == os.CLD_EXITED and info.si_status == 0
+

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""GLM-5.3-Flash KDA layers on FlashInfer's kernels: the fused decode (conv +
+SiLU, the recurrence and the gated RMSNorm in one launch) and the CuTe DSL
+chunked prefill.
+
+Each test runs the same layer, weights, caches and step once on the Triton
+path FlashInfer replaces and once on FlashInfer: conv states must match
+exactly, recurrent states and outputs within kernel rounding, and null or
+unused slots must stay untouched.
+"""
+
+from math import prod
+from typing import Any
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+from transformers import Glm5NextTextConfig
+
+from tests.v1.attention.utils import create_vllm_config
+from vllm.config import SpeculativeConfig, VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
+from vllm.forward_context import set_forward_context
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.mamba_utils import get_conv_state_layout
+from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_utils import default_weight_loader
+from vllm.models.glm5next.common.kda import (
+    Glm5NextLinearAttention,
+    _is_flashinfer_kda_prefill_supported,
+)
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.utils.torch_utils import set_default_torch_dtype
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.gdn_attn import GDNAttentionMetadata
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.utils import compute_causal_conv1d_metadata
+
+if not current_platform.is_cuda():
+    pytest.skip("FlashInfer KDA kernels are CUDA-only", allow_module_level=True)
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.usefixtures("dist_init")
+
+HIDDEN = 256
+D, W = 128, 4
+NUM_SLOTS = 24
+PREFIX = "model.layers.0.self_attn"
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def model_dir(tmp_path_factory) -> str:
+    """A one-layer GLM-5.3-Flash config; the layer needs no checkpoint."""
+    path = tmp_path_factory.mktemp("glm5next")
+    config = Glm5NextTextConfig(
+        hidden_size=HIDDEN, num_hidden_layers=1, layer_types=["linear_attention"]
+    )
+    config.architectures = ["Glm5NextForCausalLM"]
+    config.save_pretrained(path)
+    return str(path)
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def conv_state_layout(request, monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT", request.param)
+    get_conv_state_layout.cache_clear()
+    yield request.param
+    get_conv_state_layout.cache_clear()
+
+
+def _make_layer(
+    model_dir: str,
+    num_heads: int,
+    decode: str = "triton",
+    prefill: str = "triton",
+    num_spec: int = 0,
+    state_dtype: torch.dtype = torch.float32,
+) -> tuple[Glm5NextLinearAttention, VllmConfig]:
+    """A layer with seeded weights and caches, post-processed as after a load."""
+    vllm_config = create_vllm_config(
+        model_name=model_dir,
+        dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        hf_config_override={"linear_num_heads": num_heads},
+    )
+    vllm_config.cache_config.mamba_ssm_cache_dtype = (
+        "float32" if state_dtype == torch.float32 else "bfloat16"
+    )
+    vllm_config.additional_config = {
+        "kda_decode_backend": decode,
+        "kda_prefill_backend": prefill,
+    }
+    if num_spec:
+        vllm_config.speculative_config = SpeculativeConfig(
+            method="ngram", num_speculative_tokens=num_spec
+        )
+    with (
+        set_current_vllm_config(vllm_config),
+        set_default_torch_dtype(torch.bfloat16),
+        torch.device("cuda"),
+    ):
+        layer = Glm5NextLinearAttention(
+            vllm_config.model_config.hf_text_config, vllm_config, PREFIX
+        )
+
+    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(0)
+    for param in layer.parameters():
+        weight = torch.randn(param.shape, device="cuda", generator=g)
+        default_weight_loader(param, weight / param.shape[-1] ** 0.5)
+    heads = torch.linspace(1, 16, layer.local_num_heads, device="cuda")
+    default_weight_loader(layer.A_log, heads.log().view_as(layer.A_log))
+    layer.o_norm.weight.data.add_(1)
+    layer.process_weights_after_loading()
+
+    shapes, dtypes = layer.get_state_shape(), layer.get_state_dtype()
+    page_bytes = sum(prod(s) * d.itemsize for s, d in zip(shapes, dtypes))
+    layer.bind_kv_cache(
+        torch.zeros(NUM_SLOTS, 1, 1, page_bytes, dtype=torch.int8, device="cuda")
+    )
+    for cache, scale in zip(layer.kv_cache, (1.0, 0.2)):
+        cache.copy_(scale * torch.randn(cache.shape, device="cuda", generator=g))
+    return layer, vllm_config
+
+
+def _require_flashinfer_decode(layer: Glm5NextLinearAttention) -> None:
+    if layer.kda_decode_backend != "flashinfer":
+        pytest.skip("FlashInfer fused KDA decode does not support this config")
+
+
+def _require_flashinfer_prefill(state_dtype: torch.dtype) -> None:
+    if not _is_flashinfer_kda_prefill_supported(D, torch.bfloat16, state_dtype, -5.0):
+        pytest.skip("FlashInfer KDA prefill does not support this platform")
+
+
+def _hidden(num_tokens: int, seed: int = 1) -> torch.Tensor:
+    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed)
+    return torch.randn(num_tokens, HIDDEN, device="cuda", generator=g).bfloat16()
+
+
+def _forward(
+    layer: Glm5NextLinearAttention,
+    vllm_config: VllmConfig,
+    meta: GDNAttentionMetadata,
+    hidden: torch.Tensor,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    positions = torch.arange(hidden.size(0), device="cuda")
+    with (
+        set_current_vllm_config(vllm_config),
+        set_forward_context({PREFIX: meta}, vllm_config),
+    ):
+        return layer(hidden, positions)
+
+
+def _prefill_fields(
+    qsl_cpu: torch.Tensor,
+    num_decodes: int,
+    indices: torch.Tensor,
+    has_initial_state: torch.Tensor,
+) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """The prefill rows' metadata, rebased past the leading decode rows."""
+    qsl = qsl_cpu.cuda()
+    nums_dict, batch_ptr, token_chunk_offset_ptr = compute_causal_conv1d_metadata(
+        qsl_cpu, device=qsl.device
+    )
+    return dict(
+        has_initial_state=has_initial_state,
+        nums_dict=nums_dict,
+        batch_ptr=batch_ptr,
+        token_chunk_offset_ptr=token_chunk_offset_ptr,
+        prefill_query_start_loc=qsl[num_decodes:] - num_decodes,
+        prefill_state_indices=indices[num_decodes:],
+        prefill_has_initial_state=has_initial_state[num_decodes:],
+    )
+
+
+def _non_spec_metadata(
+    query_lens: list[int],
+    num_decodes: int,
+    slots: list[int],
+    has_state: list[bool],
+    block_table_width: int = 1,
+) -> GDNAttentionMetadata:
+    """Decodes first, then prefills. The slot indices are column 0 of a
+    `[N, block_table_width]` block table (a strided view when wider, as with
+    speculative decoding)."""
+    qsl_cpu = torch.tensor([0, *torch.tensor(query_lens).cumsum(0).tolist()]).int()
+    block_table = torch.zeros(
+        len(slots), block_table_width, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"
+    )
+    block_table[:, 0] = torch.tensor(slots, dtype=torch.int32)
+    indices = block_table[:, 0]
+    has_initial_state = torch.tensor(has_state, device="cuda")
+    num_tokens = int(qsl_cpu[-1])
+    prefill: dict[str, Any] = {}
+    if num_decodes < len(query_lens):
+        prefill = _prefill_fields(qsl_cpu, num_decodes, indices, has_initial_state)
+    return GDNAttentionMetadata(
+        num_prefills=len(query_lens) - num_decodes,
+        num_prefill_tokens=num_tokens - num_decodes,
+        num_decodes=num_decodes,
+        num_decode_tokens=num_decodes,
+        num_spec_decodes=0,
+        num_spec_decode_tokens=0,
+        num_actual_tokens=num_tokens,
+        non_spec_query_start_loc=qsl_cpu.cuda(),
+        non_spec_state_indices_tensor=indices,
+        **prefill,
+    )
+
+
+def _spec_metadata(
+    num_spec: int,
+    accepted: list[int],
+    prefill_lens: list[int],
+    slots: list[list[int]],
+) -> GDNAttentionMetadata:
+    """Draft-verify rows first (1 + num_spec tokens each), then prefills."""
+    T = 1 + num_spec
+    num_spec_rows = len(accepted)
+    lens = [T] * num_spec_rows + prefill_lens
+    is_spec = torch.tensor([1] * num_spec_rows + [0] * len(prefill_lens)).bool()
+    token_is_spec = torch.repeat_interleave(is_spec, torch.tensor(lens))
+    prefill: dict[str, Any] = {}
+    if prefill_lens:
+        qsl_cpu = torch.tensor(
+            [0, *torch.tensor(prefill_lens).cumsum(0).tolist()]
+        ).int()
+        indices = torch.tensor(
+            [s[0] for s in slots[num_spec_rows:]], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"
+        )
+        has_initial_state = torch.tensor([False, True], device="cuda")[
+            : len(prefill_lens)
+        ]
+        prefill = _prefill_fields(qsl_cpu, 0, indices, has_initial_state)
+        prefill.update(
+            non_spec_query_start_loc=prefill["prefill_query_start_loc"],
+            non_spec_state_indices_tensor=indices,
+        )
+    return GDNAttentionMetadata(
+        num_prefills=len(prefill_lens),
+        num_prefill_tokens=sum(prefill_lens),
+        num_decodes=0,
+        num_decode_tokens=0,
+        num_spec_decodes=num_spec_rows,
+        num_spec_decode_tokens=T * num_spec_rows,
+        num_actual_tokens=sum(lens),
+        spec_query_start_loc=torch.arange(
+            0, T * num_spec_rows + 1, T, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"
+        ),
+        spec_state_indices_tensor=torch.tensor(
+            slots[:num_spec_rows], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"
+        ),
+        spec_sequence_masks=is_spec.cuda(),
+        spec_token_indx=token_is_spec.nonzero().flatten().cuda(),
+        non_spec_token_indx=(~token_is_spec).nonzero().flatten().cuda(),
+        num_accepted_tokens=torch.tensor(accepted, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
+        **prefill,
+    )
+
+
+def _run_both(
+    flashinfer: tuple[Glm5NextLinearAttention, VllmConfig],
+    triton: tuple[Glm5NextLinearAttention, VllmConfig],
+    meta: GDNAttentionMetadata,
+    hidden: torch.Tensor,
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Runs the step on both layers. Both run the same conv kernels, so the
+    conv states must match exactly. Returns the outputs and recurrent states
+    (FlashInfer's first)."""
+    out_t = _forward(*triton, meta, hidden)
+    out_f = _forward(*flashinfer, meta, hidden)
+    (conv_t, state_t), (conv_f, state_f) = triton[0].kv_cache, flashinfer[0].kv_cache
+    torch.testing.assert_close(conv_f, conv_t, atol=0, rtol=0)
+    return out_f, out_t, state_f, state_t
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_backend_selection(model_dir):
+    """`auto` runs GLM-5.3's decode shapes (64 heads at TP1, 16 at TP4) on
+    FlashInfer on SM10x, keeps Triton for 8-head draft-verify rows, and an
+    explicit `flashinfer` fails at startup where it is unsupported."""
+    if not current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100):
+        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="SM10x"):
+            _make_layer(model_dir, 64, decode="flashinfer")
+        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="SM100/SM103/SM107"):
+            _make_layer(model_dir, 64, prefill="flashinfer")
+        return
+    for num_heads in (16, 64):

[Quantization] Support ModelOpt INT8_PB_WO routed experts (#66717)

Signed-off-by: Chenjie Luo <chenjiel@nvidia.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

@@ -20,19 +20,21 @@ following `quantization.quant_algo` values:
 - `W4A16_NVFP4`: weight-only ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoints with 16-bit
   activations (use `quantization="modelopt_fp4"`).
 - `MXFP8`: ModelOpt MXFP8 checkpoints (use `quantization="modelopt_mxfp8"`).
-- `INT8_PB_WO`: block-scaled INT8 weight-only linear layers with 16-bit
-  activations (use `quantization="modelopt_int8"`): a symmetric int8 `weight`
-  and a `weight_scale` per `group_size` input elements (for example 16 or 32).
-  `group_size` is required. vLLM serves these layers with its mixed-precision
-  (WNA16) kernels, such as Marlin and Humming on NVIDIA and Triton on ROCm.
-  MoE experts are not supported.
+- `INT8_PB_WO`: block-scaled INT8 weight-only linear layers and MoE experts
+  with 16-bit activations (use `quantization="modelopt_int8"`): a symmetric
+  int8 `weight` and a `weight_scale` per `group_size` input elements (for
+  example 16 or 32). `group_size` is required. vLLM serves these layers with
+  its mixed-precision (WNA16) kernels, such as Marlin and Humming on NVIDIA and
+  Triton on ROCm. MoE experts run on NVIDIA GPUs only, on the WNA16 MoE
+  kernels (Marlin, Triton, or Humming with `--moe-backend humming`).
 - `MIXED_PRECISION`: per-layer formats specified by `quantized_layers`
   (use `quantization="modelopt_mixed"`). Each layer may use any format above;
-  `INT8_PB_WO` layers take their own `group_size`. A token embedding marked
-  `W4A16_NVFP4` stays packed and only the looked-up rows are dequantized; the
-  model must build its embedding with the checkpoint prefix, as Nemotron-H does.
-  Such an embedding cannot be tied to the LM head, so checkpoints that tie it
-  are rejected.
+  `INT8_PB_WO` layers take their own `group_size`. `INT8_PB_WO` routed
+  experts must use it for every expert and projection of their MoE layer, with
+  one `group_size`. A token embedding marked `W4A16_NVFP4` stays packed and only
+  the looked-up rows are dequantized; the model must build its embedding with
+  the checkpoint prefix, as Nemotron-H does. Such an embedding cannot be tied to
+  the LM head, so checkpoints that tie it are rejected.
 
 For per-tensor `FP8`, vLLM converts E4M3FN weights and scales to E4M3FNUZ
 when required by the GPU, for example on AMD MI300.

+        for key, value in params.items()
+    )
+    return (
+        f" to={emitted or name}{MESSAGE}<atem:function_calls>\n"
+        f'<atem:invoke name="{emitted or name}">\n{body}</atem:invoke>\n'
+        "</atem:function_calls>"
+    )

+def _tokens(text: str) -> list[tuple[int, str]]:
+    tokens: list[tuple[int, str]] = []
+    i = 0
+    while i < len(text):
+        marker = next((m for m in VOCAB if text.startswith(m, i)), None)
+        if marker is not None:
+            tokens.append((VOCAB[marker], marker))
+            i += len(marker)
+        else:
+            tokens.append((ord(text[i]), text[i]))
+            i += 1
+    return tokens
+
+
+def _muse_parser(tokens: list[tuple[int, str]], tools: list[dict] | None = None):
+    parser_cls = ParserManager.get_parser(

+        return reasoning or "", content or "", found
+    output = collect_output(

+        )

+    found = [(c["name"], json.loads(c["arguments"])) for c in output.tool_calls]

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Muse Spark parser: recipient-routed messages parsed by one state machine.
+
+Muse Spark writes an assistant turn as a sequence of messages::
+
+    to=self<|message|>...reasoning...<|eom|><|start|>assistant
+    to=get_weather<|message|><atem:function_calls>
+    <atem:invoke name="get_weather">
+    <atem:parameter name="city">Paris</atem:parameter>
+    </atem:invoke>
+    </atem:function_calls><|eom|><|start|>assistant
+    to=user<|message|>...final answer...<|eot|>
+
+The recipient before `<|message|>` routes each body: `self` or none is
+reasoning, `user` and `commentary` are content, `developer` is dropped, and
+any other recipient is a tool. The model may write `to=NAME<|message|>` right
+after a body without `<|eom|>`, so a trailing `to=NAME` in a body is held back.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import functools
+import json
+from collections.abc import Iterable, Sequence
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+import regex as re
+
+from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import ChatCompletionToolsParam
+from vllm.parser.engine.events import EventType, SemanticEvent
+from vllm.parser.engine.parser_engine import ParserEngine
+from vllm.parser.engine.parser_engine_config import (
+    ParserEngineConfig,
+    ParserState,
+    Transition,
+)
+from vllm.parser.engine.streaming_parser_engine import StreamingParserEngine
+from vllm.tool_parsers.schema_types import ParameterTypesCache, convert_value
+from vllm.tool_parsers.utils import find_tool_name, get_function_tools
+from vllm.v1.token_buffer import rfind_tokens
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.tokenizers import TokenizerLike
+    from vllm.tool_parsers.abstract_tool_parser import Tool
+
+START = "<|start|>"
+MESSAGE = "<|message|>"
+EOM = "<|eom|>"
+EOT = "<|eot|>"
+
+_RECIPIENT_RE = re.compile(r"to=([A-Za-z0-9_.\-]+)\s*$")
+_HEADER_TAIL_RE = re.compile(r"(?:t|to|to=[A-Za-z0-9_.\-]{0,256})$")
+_INVOKE_RE = re.compile(
+    r'<atem:invoke\b[^<>]*?\bname="([^"]+)"[^<>]*>(.*?)</atem:invoke>', re.DOTALL
+)
+_PARAMETER_RE = re.compile(
+    r'<atem:parameter\b[^<>]*?\bname="([^"]+)"[^<>]*?>(.*?)</atem:parameter>',
+    re.DOTALL,
+)
+_INVOKE_END = "</atem:invoke>"
+_BODY_STATES = frozenset({ParserState.CONTENT, ParserState.REASONING})
+_MAX_HEADER_TOKENS = 64
+
+
+def _route_header(header: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
+    match = _RECIPIENT_RE.search(header)
+    recipient = match.group(1) if match else None
+    if recipient in (None, "self"):
+        return "REASONING_HEADER", recipient
+    if recipient in ("user", "commentary"):
+        return "CONTENT_HEADER", recipient
+    if recipient == "developer":
+        return "DROPPED_HEADER", recipient
+    return "TOOL_HEADER", recipient
+
+
+def _decode_value(raw: str) -> object:
+    try:
+        return json.loads(raw)
+    except ValueError:
+        return raw
+
+
+@functools.cache
+def muse_config() -> ParserEngineConfig:
+    routes = {
+        "REASONING_HEADER": Transition(ParserState.REASONING),
+        "CONTENT_HEADER": Transition(ParserState.CONTENT),
+        # The dropped body is buffered as header text and discarded with it.
+        "DROPPED_HEADER": Transition(ParserState.MESSAGE_HEADER),
+        "TOOL_HEADER": Transition(
+            ParserState.TOOL_PREAMBLE, (EventType.REASONING_END,)
+        ),
+        "START": Transition(ParserState.MESSAGE_HEADER),
+        # Content keeps the bodies after a tool message when the tool pass
+        # re-parses the reasoning pass's content.
+        "EOM": Transition(ParserState.CONTENT),
+        "EOT": Transition(ParserState.CONTENT),
+    }
+    markers = {"START": START, "MSG": MESSAGE, "EOM": EOM, "EOT": EOT}
+    return ParserEngineConfig(
+        name="muse",
+        terminals=markers,
+        token_id_terminals=markers,
+        transitions={
+            (state, terminal): transition
+            for state in (
+                ParserState.MESSAGE_HEADER,
+                ParserState.REASONING,
+                ParserState.CONTENT,
+                ParserState.TOOL_PREAMBLE,
+            )
+            for terminal, transition in routes.items()
+        },
+        initial_state=ParserState.MESSAGE_HEADER,
+        stream_arg_deltas=False,
+        tool_args_json=False,
+        strip_trailing_reasoning_whitespace=False,
+    )
+
+
+class MuseStreamingParserEngine(StreamingParserEngine):
+    def reset(self, initial_state: ParserState | None = None) -> None:
+        super().reset(initial_state)
+        self._header_tail = ""
+        self._header_tail_token_count = 0
+        self._tool_body = ""
+        self._tool_body_pos = 0
+        self._routed_header = False
+
+    def finish(self) -> list[SemanticEvent]:
+        events = self._process_scanner_items(self._scanner.flush_pending())
+        events.extend(self._process_lex_tokens(self._lexer.flush()))
+        events.extend(self._flush_header_tail())
+        events.extend(self._flush_unframed_text())
+        self._message_header_buffer = ""
+        self._message_header_token_count = 0
+        self._tool_body = ""
+        self._tool_body_pos = 0
+        self._record_reasoning_tokens(events)
+        return events
+
+    def _on_terminal(
+        self, terminal: str, value: str, token_count: int = 0
+    ) -> list[SemanticEvent]:
+        events: list[SemanticEvent] = []
+        if terminal == "MSG":
+            self._routed_header = True
+            terminal, recipient = _route_header(self._take_header(events))
+            # The tool pass routes the forwarded header again.
+            if recipient is not None:
+                value = f"to={recipient}{value}"
+        else:
+            events.extend(self._flush_unframed_text())
+        events.extend(self._flush_header_tail())
+        if (
+            self.state is ParserState.TOOL_PREAMBLE
+            and (ParserState.TOOL_PREAMBLE, terminal) in self.config.transitions
+        ):
+            self._tool_body = ""
+            self._tool_body_pos = 0
+        events.extend(super()._on_terminal(terminal, value, token_count))
+        return events
+
+    def _emit_for_state(self, text: str, token_count: int = 0) -> list[SemanticEvent]:
+        if self.state is ParserState.TOOL_PREAMBLE:
+            return self._feed_tool_body(text)
+        if self.state not in _BODY_STATES:
+            return super()._emit_for_state(text, token_count)
+        text = self._header_tail + text
+        token_count += self._header_tail_token_count
+        tail = _HEADER_TAIL_RE.search(text)
+        split = tail.start() if tail is not None else len(text)
+        self._header_tail = text[split:]
+        if not split:
+            self._header_tail_token_count = token_count
+            return []
+        self._header_tail_token_count = 0
+        return super()._emit_for_state(text[:split], token_count)
+
+    def _take_header(self, events: list[SemanticEvent]) -> str:
+        if self.state is ParserState.MESSAGE_HEADER:
+            return self._message_header_buffer
+        if self.state is ParserState.TOOL_PREAMBLE:
+            return self._tool_body
+        header = self._header_tail
+        if not _RECIPIENT_RE.fullmatch(header):
+            return ""
+        events.extend(super()._emit_for_state("", self._header_tail_token_count))
+        self._header_tail = ""
+        self._header_tail_token_count = 0
+        return header
+
+    def _flush_unframed_text(self) -> list[SemanticEvent]:
+        if (
+            self.state is not ParserState.MESSAGE_HEADER
+            or self._routed_header
+            or not self._message_header_buffer
+        ):
+            return []
+        text = self._message_header_buffer
+        token_count = self._message_header_token_count
+        self._message_header_buffer = ""
+        self._message_header_token_count = 0
+        self.state = ParserState.CONTENT
+        return self._emit_for_state(text, token_count) + self._flush_header_tail()
+
+    def _flush_header_tail(self) -> list[SemanticEvent]:
+        tail, token_count = self._header_tail, self._header_tail_token_count
+        if not tail:
+            return []
+        self._header_tail = ""
+        self._header_tail_token_count = 0
+        return super()._emit_for_state(tail, token_count)
+
+    def _feed_tool_body(self, text: str) -> list[SemanticEvent]:
+        searched = len(self._tool_body)
+        self._tool_body += text
+        events: list[SemanticEvent] = []
+        if self._tool_body.find(_INVOKE_END, max(searched - len(_INVOKE_END), 0)) < 0:
+            return events
+        for match in _INVOKE_RE.finditer(self._tool_body, self._tool_body_pos):
+            self._tool_body_pos = match.end()
+            self.tool_index += 1
+            events.extend(
+                SemanticEvent(event_type, value=event_value, tool_index=self.tool_index)
+                for event_type, event_value in (
+                    (EventType.TOOL_CALL_START, ""),
+                    (EventType.TOOL_NAME, match.group(1)),
+                    (EventType.ARG_VALUE_CHUNK, match.group(0)),
+                    (EventType.TOOL_CALL_END, ""),
+                )
+            )
+        return events
+
+
+class MuseParser(ParserEngine):
+    _streaming_engine_cls = MuseStreamingParserEngine
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        tokenizer: TokenizerLike,
+        tools: list[Tool] | None = None,
+        **kwargs,
+    ) -> None:
+        kwargs.setdefault("parser_engine_config", muse_config())
+        super().__init__(tokenizer, tools, **kwargs)
+        self._has_reasoning = True
+        self._reasoning_ended = False
+        self._arg_converter = self._convert_args
+        self._parameter_types = ParameterTypesCache()
+        vocab = self.vocab
+        self._message_ids = (vocab.get(MESSAGE),)
+        self._start_id = vocab.get(START)
+        self._boundary_ids = tuple(
+            vocab.get(token) for token in (START, MESSAGE, EOM, EOT)
+        )
+
+    def is_reasoning_end(self, input_ids: Sequence[int]) -> bool:
+        pos = len(input_ids)
+        while (pos := rfind_tokens(input_ids, self._message_ids, stop=pos)) >= 0:
+            ended = self._header_ends_reasoning(input_ids, pos)
+            if ended is not None:
+                return ended
+        return False
+
+    def is_reasoning_end_streaming(
+        self, input_ids: Sequence[int], delta_ids: Iterable[int]
+    ) -> bool:
+        pos = len(input_ids)
+        start = max(pos - len(list(delta_ids)), 0)
+        while (pos := rfind_tokens(input_ids, self._message_ids, start, pos)) >= 0:
+            if self._header_ends_reasoning(input_ids, pos):
+                return True
+        return False
+
+    def _header_ends_reasoning(self, input_ids: Sequence[int], pos: int) -> bool | None:
+        """True for a tool message, False for another role's message, else None."""
+        start = max(pos - _MAX_HEADER_TOKENS, 0)
+        boundary = rfind_tokens(input_ids, self._boundary_ids, start, pos)
+        begin = boundary + 1 if boundary >= 0 else start
+        header = self.model_tokenizer.decode(list(input_ids[begin:pos]))
+        if (
+            boundary >= 0
+            and input_ids[boundary] == self._start_id
+            and not header.startswith("assistant")
+        ):
+            return False
+        return True if _route_header(header)[0] == "TOOL_HEADER" else None
+
+    def extract_content_ids(self, input_ids: list[int]) -> list[int]:
+        return []
+
+    def count_reasoning_tokens(self, token_ids: Sequence[int]) -> int:
+        """Count reasoning-body tokens from the ids alone.
+
+        Counting streamed text events undercounts when the detokenizer holds
+        text back (stop strings, partial UTF-8) while ids advance.
+        """
+        count = 0
+        header_start = 0
+        in_reasoning = False
+        for i, token_id in enumerate(token_ids):
+            if token_id in self._message_ids:
+                header = self.model_tokenizer.decode(list(token_ids[header_start:i]))
+                in_reasoning = _route_header(header)[0] == "REASONING_HEADER"
+                header_start = i + 1
+            elif token_id in self._boundary_ids:
+                in_reasoning = False
+                header_start = i + 1
+            elif in_reasoning:
+                count += 1
+        return count
+
+    def _handle_tool_name(self, event: SemanticEvent) -> None:
+        self._tool_slots[event.tool_index].name += self._registered_name(event.value)
+
+    def _registered_name(self, name: str) -> str:
+        """Map `NAME.<suffix>` back to a registered bare `NAME`.
+
+        The chat template renders a bare tool as `"NAME.*"`, so the model may
+        fill in any suffix (`Bash.Bash`, `Bash.command`, `Glob.`). The doubled
+        form always collapses; other suffixes collapse only when no registered
+        name lives under `NAME.`, where the suffix may name a missing sibling.
+        """
+        if not self._tools or find_tool_name(self._tools, name):
+            return name
+        head, sep, tail = name.partition(".")
+        if not sep or not find_tool_name(self._tools, head):
+            return name
+        names = (
+            tool.function.name
+            if isinstance(tool, ChatCompletionToolsParam)
+            else tool.name
+            for tool in get_function_tools(self._tools)
+        )
+        if head != tail and any(n.startswith(f"{head}.") for n in names):
+            return name
+        return head
+
+    def _convert_args(self, raw_args: str, partial: bool) -> str:
+        match = _INVOKE_RE.match(raw_args)
+        if match is None:
+            return "{}"
+        properties, extra = self._parameter_types.for_tools(self._tools).get(
+            self._registered_name(match.group(1)), ({}, None)
+        )
+        arguments = {
+            key: convert_value(raw, properties.get(key, extra), _decode_value)
+            for key, raw in _PARAMETER_RE.findall(match.group(2))
+        }
+        return json.dumps(arguments, ensure_ascii=False)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""MaskedDiffusionSampler (Nemotron Labs Diffusion) reports logprobs on the
+commit step without host syncs, except for top-k wider than its stash."""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import numpy as np
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+import vllm.utils.gpu_sync_debug as gsd
+from vllm.model_executor.models import nemotron_dllm as nd
+from vllm.sampling_params import SamplingParams
+from vllm.utils.gpu_sync_debug import with_gpu_sync_check
+from vllm.utils.torch_utils import set_random_seed
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.states import SamplingStates
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="requires CUDA")
+
+DEVICE = "cuda"
+CANVAS_LEN = 8
+
+
+def _make_sampler(params, vocab, mask, max_logprobs):
+    num_reqs = len(params)
+    states = nd.NemotronLabsDiffusionRequestStates(
+        max_num_reqs=num_reqs,
+        canvas_length=CANVAS_LEN,
+        mask_token_id=mask,
+        max_denoising_steps=2,
+        device=torch.device(DEVICE),
+    )
+    base = SimpleNamespace(
+        sampling_states=SamplingStates(num_reqs, vocab),
+        req_states=SimpleNamespace(
+            draft_tokens=torch.zeros(
+                num_reqs, CANVAS_LEN, dtype=torch.int64, device=DEVICE
+            )
+        ),
+    )
+    sampler = nd.MaskedDiffusionSampler(
+        sampler=base,
+        vocab_size=vocab,
+        diffusion_states=states,
+        selection_policy="leftmost",
+        max_logprobs=max_logprobs,
+    )
+    # Slots start denoising an all-mask canvas.
+    for i, p in enumerate(params):
+        sampler.add_request(i, p)
+    sampler.apply_staged_writes()
+    return sampler
+
+
+def _make_batch(num_reqs):
+    cu = np.arange(num_reqs + 1, dtype=np.int64) * CANVAS_LEN
+    qsl_np = cu.astype(np.int32)
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        num_reqs=num_reqs,
+        num_draft_tokens=CANVAS_LEN,
+        idx_mapping_np=np.arange(num_reqs, dtype=np.intp),
+        idx_mapping=torch.arange(num_reqs, dtype=torch.int64, device=DEVICE),
+        cu_num_logits_np=cu,
+        query_start_loc_np=qsl_np,
+        query_start_loc=torch.from_numpy(qsl_np).to(DEVICE),
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def sync_check_error(monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(gsd, "_SYNC_CHECK_MODE", "error")
+    monkeypatch.setattr(gsd, "_sync_check_enabled", False)
+    gsd.enable_gpu_sync_check()
+    # Test logprobs independently of Inductor; model tests cover compilation.
+    with torch.compiler.set_stance("force_eager"):
+        yield
+
+
+def _denoise_and_commit(sampler, num_reqs, vocab, mask):
+    """Run two denoising steps, then the commit step.
+
+    Leftmost reveal over two steps unmasks the first half of each canvas on
+    the first step and the rest on the second, where the canvas converges.
+    Return the commit step's output and both steps' log-softmax.
+    """
+    set_random_seed(0)
+    step = with_gpu_sync_check(sampler)
+    batch = _make_batch(num_reqs)
+    log_softmax = []
+    for _ in range(2):
+        logits = torch.randn(num_reqs * CANVAS_LEN, vocab, device=DEVICE)
+        logits[:, mask] = float("-inf")
+        assert int(step(logits, batch).num_sampled.sum()) == 0
+        log_softmax.append(logits.view(num_reqs, CANVAS_LEN, vocab).log_softmax(-1))
+    out = step(torch.randn_like(logits), batch)
+    assert out.num_sampled.tolist() == [CANVAS_LEN] * num_reqs
+    return out, [lsm.cpu() for lsm in log_softmax]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "num_logprobs",
+    [[None, 0, 2, 5], [2, 5, 3, 5]],
+    ids=["mixed", "all_topk"],
+)
+def test_mixed_logprobs_reach_the_commit_step_without_a_host_sync(
+    sync_check_error, num_logprobs
+):
+    """A batch mixing no logprobs, logprobs=0 and top-k widths reports each
+    request's own logprobs on its commit step. logprobs=0 reports each
+    token's logprob on the step it was revealed; top-k comes from the
+    converging step. The host never learns which slots converged or commit,
+    so no step syncs with the GPU. A batch where every request asks for
+    top-k takes the path that skips the logits copy."""
+    vocab, mask = 64, 63
+    params = [SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, logprobs=k) for k in num_logprobs]
+    sampler = _make_sampler(params, vocab, mask, max_logprobs=20)
+    out, (first, converged) = _denoise_and_commit(sampler, len(params), vocab, mask)
+
+    half = CANVAS_LEN // 2
+    lists = out.logprobs_tensors.tolists()
+    for i, k in enumerate(num_logprobs):
+        revealed = torch.cat((first[i, :half], converged[i, half:]))
+        tokens = out.sampled_token_ids[i].to(torch.int64).cpu()
+        assert torch.equal(tokens, revealed.argmax(-1))
+        if k is None:
+            continue
+        lp = lists.slice_request(i, CANVAS_LEN)
+        assert lp.logprob_token_ids[:, 0].tolist() == tokens.tolist()
+        if k == 0:
+            # Greedy reveals the argmax, so its rank is 1.
+            assert (lp.sampled_token_ranks == 1).all()
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                torch.from_numpy(lp.logprobs[:, 0]), revealed.max(-1).values
+            )
+            continue
+        selected = converged[i].gather(-1, tokens[:, None])
+        ranks = (converged[i] >= selected).sum(-1)
+        assert lp.sampled_token_ranks.tolist() == ranks.tolist()
+        torch.testing.assert_close(

+class FakeGpu:
+    """A CUDA stream whose progress the test controls."""
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.now_ms = 0.0
+        self.events: list[FakeEvent] = []
+
+    def run(self, ms: float = 1.0):
+        """Complete everything recorded so far, one event every `ms`."""
+        for event in self.events:
+            self.now_ms += ms
+            event.completed_ms = self.now_ms
+        self.events.clear()
+
+
+class FakeEvent:
+    gpu: FakeGpu
+
+    def __init__(self, enable_timing=False):
+        self.completed_ms = None
+
+    def record(self):
+        self.gpu.events.append(self)
+
+    def query(self):
+        return self.completed_ms is not None
+
+    def elapsed_time(self, end):
+        if self.completed_ms is None or end.completed_ms is None:
+            raise RuntimeError("Both events must be completed")
+        return end.completed_ms - self.completed_ms
+
+
+class FakeAsyncOutput(AsyncModelRunnerOutput):
+    def get_output(self):
+        return ModelRunnerOutput(req_ids=[])
+
+    def get_kv_connector_output(self):
+        return "kv output"

+    def __init__(self):

+        self.fail_next_step = False

+    @start_iteration_timing

+        return None
+
+    @finish_iteration_timing
+    def sample_tokens(self):
+        if self.fail_next_step:
+            self.fail_next_step = False
+            return None  # as when execute_model failed
+        return FakeAsyncOutput()
+
+    @time_dummy_batch
+    def execute_dummy_batch(self):
+        pass

+    def step(self, num_tokens=1, timed=True):
+        """Run one iteration and return the records its output carries."""
+        details = IterationDetails(num_decode_tokens=num_tokens) if timed else None
+        self.execute_model(SimpleNamespace(iteration_details=details))
+        output = self.sample_tokens()
+        return output and output.get_output().iteration_records
+
+    def completed(self):
+        """Let the GPU catch up and return the records the next reply carries."""
+        FakeEvent.gpu.run()
+        return self.iteration_timer.take_ready()
+
+

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Non-blocking GPU timing of engine iterations.
+
+An iteration is timed between two CUDA events recorded on the output worker's
+stream: one before `execute_model`, one after `sample_tokens` returns. The
+interval covers the model forward pass, sampling and speculative drafting,
+including host submission gaps.
+
+The end event is often still pending when the iteration's own output is built,
+so a finished timing leaves the worker as a record with the first reply built
+after its end event has completed: the iteration's own output, a later step's
+output or a dummy batch. No step waits for a timing, so the last iterations
+before the engine goes idle are reported once it steps again.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections import deque
+from collections.abc import Callable, Iterator
+from contextlib import contextmanager
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from functools import wraps
+from itertools import count
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.v1.core.sched.output import IterationDetails
+from vllm.v1.metrics.stats import SchedulerIterationDetails
+from vllm.v1.outputs import AsyncModelRunnerOutput, ModelRunnerOutput
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.config import VllmConfig
+    from vllm.v1.core.sched.output import SchedulerOutput
+    from vllm.v1.outputs import KVConnectorOutput
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def _drop_on_cuda_error() -> Iterator[None]:
+    """Timing must never fail a step: a CUDA error drops the affected record."""
+    try:
+        yield
+    except RuntimeError as error:
+        # The timer lives on one worker per engine, whatever its local rank.
+        logger.warning_once(
+            "Dropping a GPU iteration timing: %s", str(error), scope="process"
+        )
+
+
+def _record_event() -> torch.Event | None:
+    with _drop_on_cuda_error():
+        event = torch.Event(enable_timing=True)
+        event.record()
+        return event
+    return None
+
+
+@dataclass
+class _TimedIteration:
+    index: int
+    details: IterationDetails
+    is_dummy: bool
+    start: torch.Event
+    end: torch.Event
+
+    def read(self) -> SchedulerIterationDetails:
+        """Read the elapsed time. Both events must have completed."""
+        details = self.details
+        return SchedulerIterationDetails(
+            iteration_index=self.index,
+            num_ctx_requests=details.num_ctx_requests,
+            num_ctx_tokens=details.num_ctx_tokens,
+            num_generation_requests=details.num_generation_requests,
+            num_generation_tokens=details.num_generation_tokens,
+            elapsed_ms=self.start.elapsed_time(self.end),
+            num_encoder_inputs=details.num_encoder_inputs,
+            num_encoder_output_tokens=details.num_encoder_output_tokens,
+            is_dummy=self.is_dummy,
+        )
+
+
+class IterationTimer:
+    """Times iterations on the calling thread's CUDA stream.
+
+    Only the worker's main thread uses it, and it never waits for the GPU.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self._indices = count()
+        self._started: tuple[IterationDetails, bool, torch.Event | None] | None = None
+        self._pending: deque[_TimedIteration] = deque()
+
+    def start(self, details: IterationDetails | None, is_dummy: bool = False) -> None:
+        """Begin an iteration, dropping any that never finished.
+
+        Without a scheduling snapshot the iteration is not timed.
+        """
+        self._started = (
+            None if details is None else (details, is_dummy, _record_event())
+        )
+
+    def finish(self) -> None:
+        if self._started is None:
+            return
+        details, is_dummy, start = self._started
+        self._started = None
+        # An iteration whose timing failed keeps its index, so the gap shows.
+        index, end = next(self._indices), _record_event()
+        if start is not None and end is not None:
+            self._pending.append(_TimedIteration(index, details, is_dummy, start, end))
+
+    def take_ready(self) -> list[SchedulerIterationDetails]:
+        """Pop the oldest iterations whose GPU work has completed."""
+        records: list[SchedulerIterationDetails] = []
+        while self._pending:
+            with _drop_on_cuda_error():
+                if not self._pending[0].end.query():
+                    break
+                records.append(self._pending[0].read())
+            self._pending.popleft()
+        return records
+
+
+class _WithIterationRecords(AsyncModelRunnerOutput):
+    """A step's output that also carries completed iteration records."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        output: AsyncModelRunnerOutput,
+        records: list[SchedulerIterationDetails],
+    ) -> None:
+        self._output = output
+        self._records = records
+
+    def get_output(self) -> ModelRunnerOutput:
+        output = self._output.get_output()
+        output.iteration_records = self._records
+        return output
+
+    def get_kv_connector_output(self) -> KVConnectorOutput | None:
+        return self._output.get_kv_connector_output()
+
+
+def start_iteration_timing(execute_model: Callable) -> Callable:
+    """Decorates `Worker.execute_model` to record the iteration's start."""
+
+    @wraps(execute_model)
+    def wrapper(self, scheduler_output: SchedulerOutput, *args, **kwargs):
+        if self.iteration_timer is not None:
+            self.iteration_timer.start(scheduler_output.iteration_details)
+        return execute_model(self, scheduler_output, *args, **kwargs)
+
+    return wrapper
+
+
+def finish_iteration_timing(sample_tokens: Callable) -> Callable:
+    """Decorates `Worker.sample_tokens` to record the iteration's end.
+
+    The returned output carries the iterations that have completed by then.
+    """
+
+    @wraps(sample_tokens)
+    def wrapper(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        output = sample_tokens(self, *args, **kwargs)
+        timer = self.iteration_timer
+        # Only a deferred output ends a timed iteration: sample_tokens returns
+        # None when its execute_model failed.
+        if timer is None or not isinstance(output, AsyncModelRunnerOutput):
+            return output
+        timer.finish()
+        records = timer.take_ready()
+        return _WithIterationRecords(output, records) if records else output
+
+    return wrapper
+
+
+def time_dummy_batch(execute_dummy_batch: Callable) -> Callable:
+    """Decorates `Worker.execute_dummy_batch` to time the dummy iteration.
+
+    Returns the iterations that have completed by then.
+    """
+
+    @wraps(execute_dummy_batch)
+    def wrapper(self) -> list[SchedulerIterationDetails] | None:
+        timer = self.iteration_timer
+        if timer is None:
+            return execute_dummy_batch(self)
+        timer.start(IterationDetails(), is_dummy=True)
+        execute_dummy_batch(self)
+        timer.finish()
+        return timer.take_ready()
+
+    return wrapper
+
+
+def make_iteration_timer(vllm_config: VllmConfig, rank: int) -> IterationTimer | None:
+    """Only the worker whose output the engine reads times iterations."""
+    parallel_config = vllm_config.parallel_config
+    output_rank = parallel_config.world_size - (
+        parallel_config.tensor_parallel_size
+        * parallel_config.prefill_context_parallel_size
+    )
+    if vllm_config.gpu_iteration_timing and rank == output_rank:
+        return IterationTimer()
+    return None

+`--moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl --enable-expert-parallel` runs FlashInfer's CuTeDSL MegaMoE on SM107 (compute capability 10.7, NVIDIA Rubin) GPUs for NVFP4 and MXFP4 expert checkpoints. MXFP4 weights are used as stored and run with MXFP8 activations, whatever activation scheme the checkpoint declares. ModelOpt NVFP4 and the MXFP4 experts of DeepSeek-V4.1 are validated; other checkpoints, for example compressed-tensors, have not yet been tested on SM107. It is never selected automatically.
 
 Requirements:
 
 - The `nvshmem4py-cu13` package (`uv pip install nvshmem4py-cu13`).
 - `CUTE_DSL_ARCH=sm_107a` exported before vLLM starts.
-- `NVSHMEM_SYMMETRIC_SIZE`: `(2 * top_k + 1) * hidden_size * max_num_batched_tokens` bytes is enough; set it only if that exceeds NVSHMEM's default heap size.
+- `NVSHMEM_SYMMETRIC_SIZE`: the backend needs about `(2 * top_k + 2) * hidden_size * max_num_batched_tokens` bytes for each distinct MoE layer shape and weight format, summed. With speculative decoding the draft model's MoE layers count separately. Set it only if the sum exceeds NVSHMEM's default heap size.
 
 Behavior:
 
-- The checkpoint's activation input scales (the layer maximum over the EP group) set the activation and FC1-output quantization. A non-finite scale, or a layer whose scales are all zero, fails at load.
+- For NVFP4 experts, the checkpoint's activation input scales (the layer maximum over the EP group) set the activation and FC1-output quantization. A non-finite scale, or a layer whose scales are all zero, fails at load. MXFP4 experts have no such scales.
 - For DeepSeek-V4 routing (DeepSeek-V4 and V4.1 checkpoints), vLLM sets `FLASHINFER_SM107_MEGA_CHECK_ROUTES=0` unless it is already set, because that router can return non-finite scores on valid routes and a failed check stops the worker. This disables all of FlashInfer's SM107 route checks in the process (non-finite scores, expert ids out of range, duplicate ids), so a router bug is not caught on the device. Export `FLASHINFER_SM107_MEGA_CHECK_ROUTES=1` to enable them. Other models keep FlashInfer's default.

+def _quant_scheme_check(
+    weight_key: QuantKey, activation_key: QuantKey | None
+) -> Callable[[type[MxFp4LinearKernel | Mxfp8LinearKernel]], str | None]:
+    def check(kernel_cls: type[MxFp4LinearKernel | Mxfp8LinearKernel]) -> str | None:
+        if kernel_cls._supports_quant_scheme(weight_key, activation_key):
+            return None
+        return f"quantization scheme {weight_key}x{activation_key} not supported"
+
+    return check
+
+
+def _first_usable_kernel(
+    kernels: list[type[_LinearKernelT]],
+    config: Any,
+    activation_quant_key: QuantKey | None,
+    extra_check: Callable[[type[_LinearKernelT]], str | None] | None = None,
+) -> tuple[type[_LinearKernelT] | None, list[str]]:
+    """The first kernel in priority order that is enabled, supported, implements
+    `config` and may run `activation_quant_key`, plus why earlier ones were skipped."""
+    failure_reasons = []
+    for kernel_cls in kernels:
+        if kernel_cls.__name__ in envs.VLLM_DISABLED_KERNELS:
+            failure_reasons.append(
+                f" {kernel_cls.__name__} disabled by environment variable"
+            )
+            continue
+
+        is_supported, reason = kernel_cls.is_supported()
+        if not is_supported:
+            failure_reasons.append(f"{kernel_cls.__name__}: {reason}")
+            continue
+
+        if extra_check is not None and (reason := extra_check(kernel_cls)):
+            failure_reasons.append(f"{kernel_cls.__name__}: {reason}")
+            continue
+
+        can_implement, reason = kernel_cls.can_implement(config)
+        if not can_implement:
+            failure_reasons.append(f"{kernel_cls.__name__}: {reason}")
+            continue
+
+        if reason := _check_activation_fallback(kernel_cls, activation_quant_key):
+            failure_reasons.append(reason)
+            continue
+
+        return kernel_cls, failure_reasons
+    return None, failure_reasons
+

 A critical insight is that heartbeating must start **as soon as a request enters D's scheduler** --- not when it gets scheduled for execution. Under heavy load, a request may sit in the waiting queue for much longer than the initial lease duration, and the gap between arrival and scheduling is unbounded.
 
-To achieve this, D's connector (`NixlConnectorScheduler`) hooks into the scheduler via `on_new_request()`. When a request with `do_remote_prefill=True` arrives, the connector immediately starts tracking it for heartbeats. Requests are grouped by `remote_engine_id` for efficient batching. On each scheduler step, heartbeat metadata is packaged into `NixlConnectorMetadata` and sent to the worker, throttled by a heartbeat interval of `lease_duration // 6` (~5s).
+To achieve this, D's connector (`NixlConnectorScheduler`) hooks into the scheduler via `on_new_request()`. When a request with `do_remote_prefill=True` arrives, the connector immediately starts tracking it for heartbeats. Requests are grouped by `remote_engine_id` for efficient batching. On each scheduler step, heartbeat metadata is packaged into `NixlConnectorMetadata` and sent to the worker, throttled by a heartbeat interval of `lease_duration // 6` (~5s). A newly tracked request is heartbeated at the next step without waiting for the interval, as a router may have held it for most of its lease.
 
 Tracking stops when either the KV transfer completes (via `update_connector_output`) or the request finishes/aborts (via `request_finished`).
 
@@ -42,6 +42,85 @@ Tracking stops when either the KV transfer completes (via `update_connector_outp
 
 Heartbeat sending and processing happen **in the forward loop**, not in a background thread. This means timing is not millisecond-precise --- a long model forward pass will delay heartbeats. However, the lease durations are configured with sufficient margin: with default settings, the heartbeat interval (~5s) and lease extension (~20s) are at least an order of magnitude larger than a typical forward pass. This avoids lock complexity between threads while keeping the design simple and extensible.
 
+### Stale read protection
+
+Heartbeats only start once the request has entered D's scheduler. A request that
+a router or proxy holds *outside* D after P finished (for example while D is at
+capacity) renews nothing, so P's lease runs out and P recycles the blocks for
+new prefills. Nothing in the transport notices: a NIXL read of recycled blocks
+succeeds and loads other requests' KV cache (and, for hybrid models, their SSM
+state), which surfaces later as corrupted output or NaN logits.
+
+To close this gap, P exports the lease deadline in `kv_transfer_params`
+(`remote_blocks_expiry_time`, in P's `perf_counter` domain) together with
+`remote_lease_extension`, the number of seconds each heartbeat renews the lease
+by. Before issuing a read, D's worker rebases the deadline with the clock offset
+measured at handshake and declines the read if the deadline is within
+the safety margin of now: 5s, or the heartbeat interval
+(`kv_lease_duration / 6`) for leases shorter than 30s, so that heartbeats can
+keep a short lease alive.
+
+The heartbeats D itself sent for the request are taken into account with an
+exact model of P's renewal rule: D's scheduler ships the exported deadline and
+renewal amount along with each heartbeat batch (`HeartbeatInfo.leases`), and
+the worker applies every heartbeat it sends to a per-request lease deadline
+the way P's `_handle_heartbeat` would. A heartbeat that goes out while the
+modelled lease is still alive renews it to `send time + extension`; one that
+goes out after the lease ran out renews nothing, and neither does anything after
+it. The send time plus the safety margin stands in for the arrival time on P, so
+the model can only lag the real lease, never run ahead of it (a pause between
+heartbeats is harmless as long as the current lease, initial or renewed, covers
+it). A heartbeat round that failed to reach one of the remote ranks is not
+counted: this avoids relying on the scheduler-side aggregation that keeps the
+blocks allocated until every rank's lease has ended (consequence: with PP > 1
+notification-only agents, a permanently unreachable rank means no round is ever
+recorded for that engine, and heartbeated waits longer than the lease are
+declined).
+
+The same check runs again when the read is observed complete: if the lease may
+have run out while the transfer was in flight, the KV is discarded as if the
+read had been declined (completion is observed no earlier than it happened, so
+this only errs on the side of declining).
+
+A declined read is reported to the scheduler as `failed_recving`, counted in
+`vllm:nixl_num_declined_expired_reads` on the reading instance (the P-side
+`vllm:nixl_num_kv_expired_reqs` counts the leases that ran out), and the request
+follows `kv_load_failure_policy`: with the default `fail` it finishes with an
+error, with `recompute` D prefills it locally. Deployments whose router may hold
+requests longer than `kv_lease_duration` should raise the lease, fix the router,
+or set `"kv_load_failure_policy": "recompute"`.
+
+What this does not cover:
+
+- Peers that export no deadline or no renewal amount (older versions, fixed-TTL
+  blocks, or a router that drops the fields), or for which no clock offset is
+  known, are read as before.
+- A single heartbeat stall longer than `extension - margin` (15s with the
+  defaults) marks the modelled lease as lapsed for good, even though P may have
+  renewed it if the late heartbeat still arrived in time; the request is then
+  declined however long it is heartbeated afterwards. The shared margin
+  trades this (rare, conservative) case for simplicity.
+- A heartbeat notification that takes longer than the safety margin to reach P.
+  The model credits the renewal at send time; if P only processes the heartbeat
+  after the lease ran out, the blocks are gone and the model does not know.
+  This is the assumption the heartbeat protocol itself rests on (a heartbeat
+  delayed past the lease already lets P free the blocks); a confirmation
+  round-trip from D to P before the read would remove it and is a possible
+  follow-up.
+- Request ids containing `,`: the heartbeat payload is comma-separated, so P
+  cannot match them and never renews their leases (pre-existing). The model
+  never credits a renewal for such ids, so their reads are declined once the
+  initial lease is over.
+- The clock offset is estimated once per handshake (and again whenever the
+  remote re-registers). Both hosts' monotonic clocks are assumed to be
+  rate-disciplined (NTP/chrony); an undisciplined drift that exceeds the
+  margin over the lifetime of the pairing would defeat the check.
+- Blocks released for other reasons: P frees them as soon as the expected
+  consumers' completion notifications arrive, so replayed or duplicated
+  `kv_transfer_params` read blocks the lease model considers live; and a P
+  restarted behind the same address and engine id holds neither the lease nor
+  the data. Both are outside the lease model.
+

 ```mermaid
@@ -133,4 +212,8 @@ vllm serve <MODEL> \
   }'
 ```

+happens to a request whose remote read was declined because the lease had run out: `fail`
+ends it with an error, `recompute` prefills it locally.
